judged_text: Post#cook returns `raw` completely unfiltered when cook_method is raw_html, bypassing both the Markdown/sanitize pipeline and the Plugin::Filter :after_post_cook hook, so the invariant every Discourse render surface relies on — that `cooked` HTML was sanitized at cook time — is not enforced for imported posts. RSS item bodies (re-armed by CGI.unescapeHTML at poll_feed.rb:35, which converts <script> back to <script>) and readability-scraped embeddable-host pages (which routinely include visitor UGC) are stored as `cooked` with zero sanitization and rendered via `raw post.cooked` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 and on regular topic pages — a malicious or compromised feed executes stored XSS in the Discourse origin and steals sessions of logged-in users viewing the topic or the embed iframe.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `Post#cook` early-returning `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses the normal cooking pipeline and `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` (app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` and `raw` set to the imported HTML (lib/tasks/disqus.thor now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`; app/models/topic_embed.rb sets `raw` from readability/RSS content). `Jobs::PollFeed` also does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` before import, re-materializing HTML tags. The embed surface renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), and since `cook` returns raw for these posts, that HTML is rendered without passing through the usual sanitization/hooks. This is a verifiable stored-XSS risk introduced by the change.
